en: Taal Volcano in Batangas erupts liquid magma, which cools into solid igneous rock.
The Filipino dessert halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture of shaved ice, sweet beans, and jellies.
Burning dried abaca fibers produces ash and smoke, demonstrating a chemical change that cannot be reversed.
Water vapor condenses into liquid fog on the peaks of Mount Pulag, demonstrating a physical change.
Seawater in Manila Bay is a homogeneous solution where salt is completely dissolved in liquid water.
The lightweight, hollow bones of the Philippine eagle are a physical property that enables flight.
A traditional Philippine jeepney engine burns diesel fuel, changing it from a liquid to a gas.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River contains a heterogeneous mixture of liquid water and suspended solid sand.
The bronze statue of Jose Rizal in Luneta is a solid mixture of copper and tin.
Digesting protein from milkfish in the stomach involves a chemical change that breaks down the food.
The white sand of Boracay beach is mostly solid silicon dioxide, which has a high melting point.
Fresh tuba is a liquid solution containing water and dissolved natural sugars extracted from coconut sap.
